subject: Archaeology
title: The First Maps and Land Surveys
description: A short lesson to help you apply The First Maps and Land Surveys.

hook.text: The oldest known world map is a Babylonian clay tablet from 600 BCE. Earth is a flat disc surrounded by ocean.

buildup.text: Babylonians also made detailed local maps showing fields, canals, and property boundaries — essential for taxation.

discovery.text: The world map places Babylon at the center with Assyria, Elam, and other lands arranged around it.

twist.text: Land survey tablets from Nippur show field areas calculated with mathematical precision — accurate to modern.

climax.text: Mapping served power. Knowing your territory's exact size meant knowing how much tax you could collect and how many.

punchline.text: The first maps were not about exploration.

quiz.question: What was the primary purpose of Babylonian land survey maps?
options: Planning military campaigns against neighboring empires
Establishing field boundaries for taxation and property rights
Guiding traders along trade routes to distant cities
